_note: Provisional E1 resolutions of two class C joint items, drafted by Lane C (Goal StegVerse-org/.github#164) as G-8 drafts behind the E0 checks. Each records a PENDING C-review that a later Claude or ChatGPT review receipt supersedes. Nothing here edits a registry, a generation, a setting or a ledger: an op that uses a resolution writes only when its own E0 checks pass, from landed bytes, on the named event.

Q-ORG-REGISTRY-GENERATION.question: how orchestration/task-registry.json (StegVerse-org/.github) declares its registry generation; the #3266 readback for org main is FAIL_CLOSED REGISTRY_GENERATION_NOT_DECLARED
Q-ORG-REGISTRY-GENERATION.resolution: the registry's genesis generation is declared by a manifest transition, ORG_REGISTRY_GENERATION_GENESIS: one sealed organization-ledger receipt (FROM_HEAD on refs/stegverse/organization-ledger, through the existing two-level append) that binds generation 0 to the registry file's exact blob as observed by a sealed #3266 readback that is FAIL_CLOSED REGISTRY_GENERATION_NOT_DECLARED for this repository. The registry file is never edited. SV_CHANGE_ADMISSION_GENESIS then reads from_registry_generation 0 from that receipt and appends at 0 + 1 = 1
Q-ORG-REGISTRY-GENERATION.consumed_by: resident-runtime/sv_change_admission_genesis.py check_base_state (REGISTRY_GENERATION_FROM_SEALED_BASE_STATE): a ledgered ORG_REGISTRY_GENERATION_GENESIS receipt for the readback's exact registry blob is E0 evidence

c_review.supersedable_by: a sealed Claude or ChatGPT review receipt naming question Q-ORG-REGISTRY-GENERATION and this resolution_sha256 (a later review receipt, posted under Q-SV-NATIVE-BOOTSTRAP on StegVerse-org/.github#167). ACCEPT fills receipt_sha256 and the resolution then also runs at E0; REVISE or DENY is answered by a successor resolution that names this one under supersedes
c_review.effect_of_a_later_deny: an admission miss (P1 admission_miss) answered by a successor resolution and successor receipts; never a retroactive un-declaration of a ledgered receipt
c_review.pending_is_not_a_refusal: at E1 the E0 checks plus this PENDING record are enough (E0_CHECKS_PLUS_LATER_RECEIPTED_REVIEW); it degrades, never stops

Q-SV-NATIVE-BOOTSTRAP.question: which existing resident or workflow event runs resident-runtime/sv_change_admission_genesis.py append on the genesis-request PR's exact head (genesis without merge)
Q-SV-NATIVE-BOOTSTRAP.resolution: the existing GitHub pull_request event (types opened, synchronize, reopened) of the same-repository genesis-request PR that changes only control/sv-merge-admission/genesis-request.json, received by this repository's existing workflow .github/workflows/sv-change-admission-genesis-validation.yml as landed on main. Because the request PR does not edit that workflow, the run uses the landed workflow bytes, so the self-trigger problem does not arise. The run takes the existing ORGANIZATION_LEDGER_LOCK (concurrency group organization-ledger) and publishes by the existing fast-forward-only push compare-and-swap that organization-ledger-merge-transfer.yml and organization-ledger-transition.yml use. In that run, org_registry_generation_genesis.py append runs first (a replay once ledgered), then sv_change_admission_genesis.py append. No dispatch, no cron, no polling, no merge, no new dependency
Q-SV-NATIVE-BOOTSTRAP.landing_form: the writer job is added to that workflow by its own admitted change (after this resolution is landed, or superseded by the review); this draft adds no writer job and the workflow stays contents: read
e0_checks: GENESIS_EVENT_IS_THE_DECLARED_EVENT (event_name, action, repository, PR number and exact head equal the genesis request's; workflow_ref names the declared workflow at refs/heads/main)
Q-SV-NATIVE-BOOTSTRAP.unknown: whether the organization's Actions default allows a same-repository pull_request job to request contents: write (UNKNOWN_NOT_AUTHENTICALLY_OBSERVED; not a settings change; observed at landing, FAIL_CLOSED LEDGER_WRITER_REFUSED if it does not)
